title: The Ledger of Vilna
premise: Cyrus Amberdale, indentured since childhood to the Vilna Trading Company, has survived by mastering which silences keep people safe. When the season's last bridge closes, trapping her in the river town with a dying master ledger-keeper, she discovers the company's books conceal a debt-forgery scheme that will strip the pearl divers of their boats — and that her own indenture papers are among the forgeries. Torn between loyalty to the company that raised her, love for a diver's son who trusts her, and the truth she can no longer unlearn, Cyrus must copy the true ledgers before the workshop is burned to hide the evidence. She finishes the work as the ice breaks, choosing truth over belonging, and walks out over the reopened bridge carrying the pages that will free them all.
about_author: Kestrel Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing merchant ledgers from Baltic river towns. Their fiction explores what ordinary clerks owe to the people their numbers describe.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. On the final day before the bridge closes for winter, Cyrus carries sealed accounts across the river one last time, watching the diver families unload their season's catch. She notices Master Ellery, the old ledger-keeper, hiding a page inside his coat. The beat: uneasy obedience — she has learned not to ask.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Assigned to assist the failing Ellery in the workshop, Cyrus learns the mechanics of double-entry bookkeeping and the quiet hierarchy of the counting house. She glimpses figures that don't reconcile — small at first, deniable. Emotional beat: pride in her competence shadowed by the first itch of doubt.

chapters.title: The Diver's Son
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Tam Voss, son of a pearl diver, delivers oyster shells to the workshop and lingers to talk with Cyrus. Their friendship, begun years ago across the workshop counter, deepens; he speaks of buying his family's boat free this spring. Beat: warmth and longing — and the first lie she tells him by omission.

chapters.title: What Ellery Kept
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Ellery, coughing blood, entrusts her with a locked drawer 'if anything happens.' Inside she finds duplicate pages showing forged debts against the diving families — including an inflated sum on the Voss boat. Beat: vertigo; the silences she mastered were built on someone else's ruin.

chapters.title: The Company's Kindness
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Factor Brannic, the company's local face, publicly forgives a diver's debt at the winter feast — theater Cyrus now recognizes. Tam sees generosity where she sees bait. They quarrel when she warns him vaguely. Beat: love strained by the asymmetry of what each knows.

chapters.title: A Death in Winter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Ellery dies, officially of his lungs; unofficially, after asking too many questions aloud. Brannic orders the workshop's older records moved 'for burning' come thaw. Cyrus realizes the evidence — and any chance to finish copying it — has a deadline. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Nightwork
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with Tam drawn in. She confesses everything to Tam and recruits him as lookout while she copies the true ledgers by lamplight after hours. Each night the risk compounds: a clerk sleeping in the loft, a missing seal. Beat: terror braided with intimacy — trust as an act of courage.

chapters.title: The Broken Seal
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. A routine audit nearly catches them; Tam covers for Cyrus with a lie of his own, then discovers his father has already signed a new 'renewed' contract he cannot read. The forgery is no longer abstract — it is his family's name. Beat: betrayal curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Fire Before Thaw
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Brannic moves the burning up; the workshop will burn early, with Cyrus conveniently inside finishing inventory. In the climax, she and Tam smuggle the completed true ledgers out through the shell cellar as smoke fills the rafters, and Cyrus chooses to leave behind her own forged indenture rather than the divers' pages. Beat: sacrifice — belonging traded for truth.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Shared POV. With the ice broken, the bridge reopens and Cyrus crosses it carrying the ledgers to the magistrate in the county seat, Tam beside her. The divers' debts are voided; her own indenture is examined and dissolved. Standing on the far bank, neither bound nor owned, she begins a new ledger of her own. Beat: release — belonging finally chosen, not assigned.
